results.title: Iran’s Execution Machine: Political Hangings Surge as Dozens Face Imminent Death
results.author: B
highlights: In the last six weeks, Iran has executed at least 22 political prisoners, including ten during the January 2026 protests, an average of one execution every two days. The Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI) found that these executions were carried out in secret and without prior notice to the families or lawyers. They followed fast-tracked and unfair trials that included torture, forced confessions, and the complete absence of due process. Dozens more people arrested during the protests have been sentenced to death following torture and forced “confessions,” and sham trials without independent lawyers. ChRI has called on governments, multilateral institutions, and UN bodies to demand an immediate moratorium on all executions in Iran, with consequences for non-compliance.

results.title: Tehran’s killing machine accelerates: Executions expose a fragile regime terrified of a restive nation
results.author: Majid Majid
highlights:
# Tehran’s killing machine accelerates: Executions expose a fragile regime terrified of a restive nation |

Published: 2026-04-26T11:53:08+00:00
Author: Majid Majid

## Summary

The Iranian regime's continued crackdown on dissidents has resulted in the death of two political prisoners over the past two days. The executions, which follow the aftermath of a massive December 2025–January 2026 nationwide uprising, are seen as a desperate domestic purge. The judiciary's news agency justified the executions by accusing Erfan Kiani of "destroying public and private property, setting fires, carrying and using Molotov cocktails, carrying cold weapons, and blocking the path of vehicles". This marks the ninth execution related to the recent uprising and the 17th political execution in the past month. The Supreme Court of Tehran has upheld the death sentences of three young rebellious youths, Ehsan Hosseinipour, Matin Mohammadi, and Erfan Amiri. Maryam Rajavi, President-elect of the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI), calls for immediate action by the international community to stop the executions and protect the lives of political prisoners.

## Story

Coming in the aftermath of the massive December 2025–January 2026 nationwide uprising that brought the clerical establishment to its knees, these executions serve as a desperate domestic purge. While the regime attempts to project power and control through these brutal hangings, in reality, it is exposing its deep-seated fear of an increasingly restive society. ## The execution of uprising protesters Early Saturday morning, on April 25, 2026, the regime’s judiciary hanged Erfan Kiani, a brave rebellious youth from Isfahan. Kiani was arrested during the recent nationwide protests. Mizan, the judiciary’s news agency, attempted to justify the execution by accusing him of “destroying public and private property, setting fires, carrying and using Molotov cocktails, carrying cold weapons, blocking the path of vehicles, and attacking agents.” The regime claimed he acted as a ringleader, stating that “by carrying pre-prepared wooden boards and tires, he facilitated setting fires in the streets” during the January uprising. The threat of execution now looms over other detained protesters. In Tehran, the regime’s Supreme Court has upheld the death sentences of three young rebellious youths: Ehsan Hosseinipour, Matin Mohammadi, and Erfan Amiri. “Forced shaving of heads, verbal abuse, and insults.”
[...]
As the Iranian regime maintains a climate of fear through “daily executions,” the campaign stressed that the Iranian people are viewed by the state as the “primary enemy.” The prisoners appealed to the international community to break the silence imposed by internet blackouts.
[...]
“It is very important and essential that in these volatile and decisive days, the freedom-loving people of Iran and all ‘No to Execution’ activists do not remain silent against the government’s suppression and act as the voice of the captives in prison and those sentenced to death.”
[...]
The statement concluded with a demand for the UN Fact-Finding Mission to take “serious action” by visiting Iranian detention centers and pressuring the government to halt the execution machine.
